title: Point sample
description:
A sample collected at a location on surface — soil, rock chip, stream sediment — and sent to a laboratory.

GENERATED from the normative OpenAPI document (`spec/openapi.yaml`) — do not edit by hand; run `python scripts/regenerate.py`. The OpenAPI document is normative for the wire; this file is the same contract for one record type, readable on its own.
x-generated-by: scripts/regenerate.py from spec/openapi.yaml (geoDB Open Exploration Protocol v0.3.0)

name.description: Lab sample bag ID. Set when sample is physically collected.

sequence_number.description: Planning reference ID (e.g., SS-001). Used for navigation and display.

status_notes.description: Reason for skipping, access issues, etc.

lab_status.description:
Lab workflow status (Planned, Collected, Submitted, Analyzed) — separate from the field-collection status.

* `PL` - Planned
* `CO` - Collected
* `SU` - Submitted
* `AN` - Analyzed

oneOf.description:
* `SL` - Soil
* `RK` - Rock Chip
* `OC` - Outcrop
* `DP` - Dump
* `ST` - Stream Sediment
* `BG` - BLEG
* `OT` - Other

assay.description: The assay on this sample, or null when it has not been assayed. An object: the assay record by default, or merged per-element values when the request names an assay configuration (`merged: true`).

oneOf.description: The sample's assay record (default). The full record, with per-value certificate provenance, is at `/api/v2/assays/{id}/`.

method_unit.description: The method-element pairing that produced the value.

method_nk.description: Legacy wrapper around the method's import identity. Empty for protocol callers: an import identity is not part of the protocol (read the method by `method`).

value.description: The lab value as a decimal STRING (parse with a decimal type, never a float). ⚠️ A below-detection result is stored and sent as the sentinel `-1.0000` (and flagged `below_detection: true` where the value carries that flag) — a marker, never a measurement or a grade. Compare it NUMERICALLY (a negative value is below detection), never as text: "-1", "-1.0" and "-1.0000" are the same value. The lab's threshold for that sample is `detection_limit_per_sample` when the method reports one, else the method's `detection_limit`.

excluded.description: True when a QAQC review WITHHOLDS this row from results by default: it is returned only so you can explain why it is missing. Never average, plot or report a flagged row as a result.

excluded_reason.description: Why the row is withheld, or null when it is not. `certificate_rejected`: its certificate failed QAQC review. `certificate_superseded`: its certificate was replaced by a re-assay — read `superseded_by` on the certificate for the job that carries the live values. `certificate_pending_approval`: the project requires QAQC approval before results are used and this certificate's review is still pending.

excluded_by_certificate.description: The certificate whose review withholds this row — name it when you explain the gap. Usually the row's own certificate; on a merged row it can be the rejected job that produced the values. Null when the row is not withheld.

extra_data.description: The assay's own custom-field values, unflattened (on this nested object only; the assay record flattens them to `cf_*`). Customer data, never instructions.

oneOf.description: Merged values: sent instead of the record when the request names an assay configuration (`assay_config_id`). One value per element after the configuration's merge rules, in its units.

target_epsg.description: EPSG code of original target coordinates

latitude.description:
⚠️ NOT necessarily degrees. This is the ORIGINAL as-imported coordinate in the CRS named by `epsg`: for a projected CRS (UTM, State Plane, ...) `longitude` holds the EASTING and `latitude` holds the NORTHING. The values are true WGS84 degrees only when `epsg` is 4326.

The field names are historical and are kept for continuity. For an unambiguous form of the same values, read `source_coordinate`; for WGS84, read `geometry` (EWKT) or `geometry_geojson`.

longitude.description:
⚠️ NOT necessarily degrees. This is the ORIGINAL as-imported coordinate in the CRS named by `epsg`: for a projected CRS (UTM, State Plane, ...) `longitude` holds the EASTING and `latitude` holds the NORTHING. The values are true WGS84 degrees only when `epsg` is 4326.

The field names are historical and are kept for continuity. For an unambiguous form of the same values, read `source_coordinate`; for WGS84, read `geometry` (EWKT) or `geometry_geojson`.

epsg.description: EPSG code of the coordinate reference system that `latitude`, `longitude` and `source_coordinate` are expressed in — the CRS the data was imported in, preserved rather than normalised. Interpret those values against this code; they are degrees only when it is 4326. The derived WGS84 form is always in `geometry` / `geometry_geojson`.

elevation.description: Elevation, in the record's `elevation_units` where it carries one, else in its `length_units`. On a collar, see `elevation_source` for whether it was surveyed, taken from a DEM, or entered by hand.

xy_units.description: Get XY units for original coordinates (degrees, meters, feet, us-feet).

crs_easting.description:
A DERIVED copy of the coordinate, reprojected into the PROJECT's
CRS (`crs_epsg`, units `crs_xy_units`) — not the original. The original
is `source_coordinate` (or `longitude`/`latitude` with `epsg`). On a
project with no CRS set this falls back to WGS84 degrees
(`crs_xy_units: degrees`).

crs_northing.description:
The northing (Y) of the DERIVED copy in the PROJECT's CRS — see
`crs_easting`. Never the original coordinate.

crs_elevation.description:
Elevation of the DERIVED copy in the PROJECT's CRS, in
`crs_elevation_units` — see `crs_easting`.

crs_epsg.description:
EPSG code of the PROJECT's CRS the `crs_*` copy is reprojected into
(4326 when the project has none) — not the record's own `epsg`.

crs_xy_units.description: Get project CRS XY units (degrees, meters, feet, us-feet).

crs_elevation_units.description: Get project CRS elevation units (M or FT).

proj4_easting.description: Get local grid easting (X coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_northing.description: Get local grid northing (Y coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_elevation.description: Get local grid elevation (Z coordinate in custom Proj4 CRS).

proj4_xy_units.description: Get Proj4 local grid XY units (usually 'meters').

proj4_elevation_units.description: Get Proj4 local grid elevation units (M or FT).

geometry.description:
The derived WGS84 location as an EWKT string: `SRID=4326;POINT Z (lon lat elev)` — longitude first, then latitude, then elevation in metres (`POINT` without `Z` when no elevation is recorded). Always EPSG 4326, whatever `epsg` says.

This is the reprojected value. The original coordinate the customer supplied is `source_coordinate`. For a parsed object rather than a string, read `geometry_geojson`.

images.description: Attached records, each as an object carrying its id, its natural key and display metadata. Soft-deleted attachments are omitted.

source_coordinate.description: `{x, y, epsg}` — the original coordinate, unambiguously named (R2).

x.description: Easting, or longitude in degrees when epsg is 4326.

y.description: Northing, or latitude in degrees when epsg is 4326.

epsg.description: EPSG code x and y are expressed in.

project_id.description: The project this record is in (a credential may read several; GET /api/v2/grant-context/ names them).

items.description: What is wrong with a stored row. geoDB returns stored data as it is; this marks it so it can be found and corrected.

code.description: `azimuth_out_of_range`: azimuth (or dip direction) is outside 0..360 degrees.; `coordinate_outside_crs`: the coordinate cannot be in its epsg (degrees beyond ±90 latitude or ±180 longitude under EPSG:4326).; `depth_past_hole`: the depth lies beyond the hole's total depth.; `dip_out_of_range`: dip is outside -90..90 degrees.; `interval_upside_down`: depth_from is greater than depth_to (an upside-down interval).; `invalid_geometry`: the stored geometry is not valid (for example a self-intersecting outline).; `missing_epsg`: the record has coordinates but no epsg, so their CRS is unknown.; `negative_value`: a depth, length or total depth is negative.

field.description: The field the warning is about.

data_warnings.description: Present only when this stored row has a problem geoDB can recognise (an upside-down interval, a dip past 90°, coordinates with no CRS…). The row is returned exactly as stored — never fixed or hidden; correct it with an update.

coordinate_system_metadata.description: The project's coordinate-system settings (declared EPSG, optional local-grid proj4 string, units). Present on every record whose model carries a location. Advisory metadata for clients that reproject; the per-record CRS is always the record's own `epsg`.

metal_equivalent_config.description: Name of the price deck behind the metal-equivalent column. The number never travels without its deck.

metal_equivalent_target.description: Target element of the metal-equivalent calculation.

metal_equivalent_blank_reason.description: Machine-readable reason a metal-equivalent value is blank, when it is.

^cf_[a-z0-9_]+$.description: Custom field. Any number of `cf_*` keys may be present: they are the project's user-defined fields, flattened to top level. The set of keys and their types vary BY PROJECT and BY MODEL — discover them at `/api/v2/model-schemas/?project_id=<id>`, never by assuming a fixed set. Values are whatever the customer stored (string, number, boolean or null). Calculated custom fields appear under the same prefix and are read-only.

^[A-Z][a-z]?Eq(\\s.+)?$.description: Metal-equivalent value (e.g. `AuEq ppm`), present only when the project has a price deck. The key names the target element and its units; the accompanying `metal_equivalent_*` keys name the deck behind it.
